dicas.texto: Você está indo bem! Quantas vezes o número 5 cabe dentro do 12 sem passar dele?
Tente dividir 12 por 5. O quociente será a sua parte inteira (m1) e o resto será o novo numerador (m2). O denominador (m3) permanece o mesmo.
O número 5 cabe duas vezes no 12 (5 + 5 = 10). Quanto sobra para chegar em 12?
Você tem 2 inteiros (10/5). Para chegar em 12/5, falta quanto? Preencha m1 com 2, m2 com o que sobrou e m3 com 5.
Lembre-se que cada unidade na reta está dividida em 5 partes iguais. Onde o número 2 se localiza?
Localize o número 2 na reta. A partir dele, conte duas das cinco pequenas marcações invisíveis para a direita.
Se cada marca vale 1/5, a segunda marca após o número 2 é o lugar correto.
Conte: 2, depois 2 e 1/5, e finalmente 2 e 2/5. O ponto deve ficar exatamente na segunda marca após o 2.

interfaceCtat.descricao: Interface FIXA do tutor (a mesma tela para todos os problemas): enunciado; pergunta "What is the fraction in the problem? Convert it to mixed fraction form if it will help you." com duas caixas numéricas (f1 em cima = numerador, f2 embaixo = denominador); botão "Convert" que abre as caixas do número misto (m1 = parte inteira, m2/m3 = fração restante; "-" quando não há); reta numérica de 0 a 3 (numline) onde o aluno marca um ponto, com encaixe em 5 partes por unidade (marcas ocultas); texto de apoio na reta: "The number hint is off in this problem!"; botão Hint; botão Done. Os passos do aluno são ações NESSES componentes (digitar nos campos, converter, marcar o ponto, concluir).

reta numérica; o aluno adiciona um ponto (marca a posição da fração)
grupo com m1/m2/m3, exibido depois de Convert
botão "Convert": abre as caixas do número misto (m1, m2, m3) para reescrever a fração
campo numérico da caixa de cima da fração (numerador)
campo numérico: parte inteira do número misto

dicas.texto: Which number tells how many total pieces Brandon gave to his friends?
Use the total number of pieces given as the numerator, the number on top of the fraction.
Look at the phrase saying that Brandon gave his friends a total of ... pieces.
Type the total number of pieces given into the top box of the fraction.
What number represents one complete pack of gum?
Use the number of equal pieces in one whole pack as the denominator, the number on the bottom.
The problem says that each pack had five pieces.
Type the number of pieces in one pack into the bottom box of the fraction.
Compare the number of pieces given with the number of pieces in one pack.
A fraction is greater than one when its numerator is greater than its denominator.
The numerator is 12 and the denominator is 5, so the fraction describes more than one whole pack.
Use the button that opens the mixed-number boxes for a fraction greater than one.
How many complete packs can be made from 12 pieces when each pack needs 5 pieces?
Divide 12 by 5. Place the whole-number quotient first, then use the remainder over the original denominator.
Two groups of 5 use 10 pieces, leaving 2 pieces that are part of another pack.
Enter the number of complete packs in m1, the leftover pieces in m2, and keep the original pack size in m3.
Use the mixed number to decide which whole-number interval contains the fraction.
Divide the numerator by the denominator to find the decimal position on the number line.
The point lies between 2 and 3, two fifths of the way after 2.
On the interval from 2 to 3, count two of the five equal fractional spaces after 2 and place the point there.
Check that the fraction, mixed number, and number-line point all describe the same amount.
Review the numerator, denominator, whole-number part, remaining numerator, remaining denominator, and marked position.
The fraction should show 12 over 5, the mixed number should show two complete packs and two fifths, and the point should be between 2 and 3.
When every field and the number-line point are complete, use the button that submits the finished problem.

hints.message: How many complete packs can be made from 12 pieces when each pack needs 5 pieces?
Divide 12 by 5. Place the whole-number quotient first, then use the remainder over the original denominator.
Two groups of 5 use 10 pieces, leaving 2 pieces that are part of another pack.
Enter the number of complete packs in m1, the leftover pieces in m2, and keep the original pack size in m3.

misconceptions.description: Aluno inverte a parte fracionária do número misto após calcular o inteiro
misconceptions.feedback: The whole-number part is correct, but the fraction was inverted. The denominator remains the original pack size, 5.

misconceptions.description: Aluno não completa a divisão total, parando no primeiro inteiro
misconceptions.feedback: You removed only one group of 5. There are still enough pieces for a second complete group.

misconceptions.description: Aluno arredonda o resultado da divisão para o próximo inteiro
misconceptions.feedback: Three complete packs would require 15 pieces, but Brandon gave only 12 pieces.

nodes.description: Mark 12/5 on the number line from 0 to 3.
nodes.instruction: Mark 12/5 on the number line from 0 to 3.

hints.message: Use the mixed number to decide which whole-number interval contains the fraction.
Divide the numerator by the denominator to find the decimal position on the number line.
The point lies between 2 and 3, two fifths of the way after 2.
On the interval from 2 to 3, count two of the five equal fractional spaces after 2 and place the point there.

misconceptions.description: Aluno trata o numerador como a posição absoluta na reta, ignorando a escala da fração
misconceptions.feedback: The numerator is not the absolute position. Because each unit is divided into fifths, 12/5 lands at 2.4 on the number line.

nodes.description: Click Done after completing the fraction, mixed number, and number-line point.
nodes.instruction: Click Done after completing the fraction, mixed number, and number-line point.

hints.message: Check that the fraction, mixed number, and number-line point all describe the same amount.
Review the numerator, denominator, whole-number part, remaining numerator, remaining denominator, and marked position.
The fraction should show 12 over 5, the mixed number should show two complete packs and two fifths, and the point should be between 2 and 3.
When every field and the number-line point are complete, use the button that submits the finished problem.
